title: Phase 2A: Enterprise Foundation
description:
Harden Relicta for multi-user enterprise deployment. The CLI, governance
engine, policy system, MCP apps, and AI providers are production-ready.
Phase 2A closes the remaining gaps: persistent storage for scaling beyond
single-machine file-based state, session-based authentication for the web
dashboard, OIDC/SSO integration for enterprise identity, a versioned REST
API surface with OpenAPI documentation, and an analytics persistence layer
so risk trends and team metrics survive restarts.

features.title: Session Authentication
features.description:
Implement JWT-based session authentication for the web dashboard.
The API key auth mode works; session mode returns 501 Not Implemented.
Add token issuance, validation, refresh, and revocation. Support
secure cookie transport for browser sessions.

requirements.title: Implement JWT token service
requirements.description:
Create a token service that issues signed JWTs with configurable
expiry, refresh tokens, and revocation via a deny list. Use
HMAC-SHA256 with a server-generated secret or RSA key pair.

requirements.title: Wire session auth into middleware
requirements.description:
Replace the TODO stub in auth.go session mode with real JWT
validation. Extract claims, map to roles (Admin, Approver,
Viewer), and populate request context.

requirements.title: Add login and logout API endpoints
requirements.description:
POST /api/auth/login (credentials → JWT + refresh token),
POST /api/auth/refresh (refresh → new JWT),
POST /api/auth/logout (revoke tokens).
Rate-limit login attempts.

requirements.title: Add session auth test coverage
requirements.description:
Unit tests for token service (issue, validate, refresh, revoke).
Integration tests for login flow, expired tokens, role mapping,
and rate limiting. Target 90%+ coverage on auth package.

features.title: OIDC / SSO Integration
features.description:
Add OpenID Connect provider support so enterprises can use their
existing identity provider (Okta, Azure AD, Google Workspace) for
dashboard authentication. Map OIDC claims to Relicta roles.

requirements.title: Add OIDC provider configuration
requirements.description:
Extend DashboardAuthConfig with OIDC fields: issuer URL,
client ID, client secret, redirect URI, scopes, and claim
mappings. Support discovery via .well-known/openid-configuration.

requirements.title: Implement OIDC authorization code flow
requirements.description:
Add /api/auth/oidc/login (redirect to IdP), /api/auth/oidc/callback
(exchange code for tokens, create session). Validate ID tokens,
extract claims, map groups to roles.

requirements.title: Map OIDC claims to Relicta roles
requirements.description:
Configurable claim-to-role mapping (e.g., groups claim "relicta-admins"
→ Admin role). Support multiple IdPs with independent mappings.
Fallback to default Viewer role for unmapped users.

requirements.title: Test OIDC flows and document setup
requirements.description:
Integration tests with a mock OIDC provider. Document IdP setup
for Okta, Azure AD, and Google Workspace with example configs.

features.title: Database Persistence Layer
features.description:
Add PostgreSQL as an optional persistence backend alongside the
existing file-based event store. Enable horizontal scaling,
concurrent access, and queryable release history. Keep file-based
as the default for single-machine use.

requirements.title: Define persistence port interface
requirements.description:
Extract a clean port interface from the file event store adapter.
Both file-based and PostgreSQL adapters implement the same interface.
Use the repository pattern from the existing hexagonal architecture.

requirements.title: Implement PostgreSQL adapter
requirements.description:
Implement the persistence port using sqlc for type-safe query
generation with pgx as the driver. Store events in an append-only
events table with JSONB payload. Add indexes for release ID,
timestamp, and event type. Use connection pooling.

requirements.title: Add database migration framework
requirements.description:
Embed SQL migrations via go:embed. Support up/down migrations
with version tracking. Add `relicta db migrate` and
`relicta db status` CLI commands. Use golang-migrate or similar.

requirements.title: Add persistence configuration
requirements.description:
Extend config schema with persistence section: backend type
(file, postgres), connection string (with env var expansion),
pool size, migration mode (auto, manual). Wire adapter selection
in container setup.

requirements.title: Add persistence layer tests
requirements.description:
Unit tests with interface mocks. Integration tests with testcontainers
for PostgreSQL. Test migration up/down, concurrent writes, event
replay, and failover to file-based when DB is unreachable.

features.title: Analytics Persistence
features.description:
Persist risk trends, governance decisions, and team metrics so the
dashboard shows historical data across restarts. Build on the
persistence port interface from the database feature.

requirements.title: Capture analytics events
requirements.description:
Emit structured analytics events for: risk evaluations, policy
decisions, approval outcomes, release durations, bump types.
Store via the persistence port (file or PostgreSQL).

requirements.title: Add analytics query endpoints
requirements.description:
GET /api/analytics/risk-trends (time-series risk scores),
GET /api/analytics/decisions (policy decision distribution),
GET /api/analytics/team (approvals per actor, release velocity).
Support date range and granularity parameters.

requirements.title: Implement analytics aggregation
requirements.description:
Pre-aggregate metrics for dashboard performance: daily/weekly/monthly
rollups for risk scores, decision counts, release frequency.
For file backend, aggregate on read. For PostgreSQL, use
materialized views or scheduled aggregation.

requirements.title: Add analytics test coverage
requirements.description:
Unit tests for event capture and aggregation logic. Integration
tests for query endpoints with seeded data. Verify both file
and PostgreSQL backends produce consistent results.

features.title: REST API Hardening
features.description:
Version the REST API, add pagination to list endpoints, generate
OpenAPI documentation, and add structured error responses. Make
the API suitable for third-party integrations.

requirements.title: Add API versioning
requirements.description:
Prefix all API routes with /api/v1/. Add version negotiation
via Accept header. Document versioning policy (additive changes
in minor, breaking changes in major).

requirements.title: Add pagination and filtering to list endpoints
requirements.description:
Cursor-based pagination for releases, events, and audit trail
endpoints. Support limit, cursor, sort, and filter query params.
Return Link headers and pagination metadata in response body.

requirements.title: Generate OpenAPI specification
requirements.description:
Annotate handlers with OpenAPI metadata. Generate spec at build
time or serve at /api/v1/openapi.json. Include authentication
schemes, error responses, and example payloads.

requirements.title: Implement structured error responses
requirements.description:
Standardize error format: {code, message, details, request_id}.
Map domain errors to HTTP status codes consistently. Add
request ID middleware for correlation.

requirements.title: Add API contract tests
requirements.description:
Integration tests verifying pagination, error formats, versioning,
and OpenAPI spec accuracy. Use golden file tests for response
shapes. Target full endpoint coverage.

features.title: Webhook Delivery Hardening
features.description:
The webhook config schema exists but the delivery engine needs
production hardening: persistent delivery queue, retry with
backoff, delivery logging, and dead-letter handling.

requirements.title: Add persistent webhook delivery queue
requirements.description:
Queue webhook deliveries for async processing. Persist pending
deliveries so they survive restarts. Process in order per
endpoint with configurable concurrency.

requirements.title: Implement retry with exponential backoff
requirements.description:
Retry failed deliveries with exponential backoff and jitter.
Respect Retry-After headers. Move to dead-letter after max
retries. Log all delivery attempts with status codes.

requirements.title: Add webhook delivery log
requirements.description:
Log delivery attempts with timestamp, endpoint, status code,
response time, and payload hash. Expose via
GET /api/v1/webhooks/:id/deliveries. Support manual re-delivery.

requirements.title: Add webhook delivery tests
requirements.description:
Unit tests for queue, retry logic, and backoff calculation.
Integration tests with httptest server simulating failures,
slow responses, and redirects.

features.title: Monorepo Workspace Orchestration
features.description: Add first-class monorepo support for governing changes across multiple packages in a single repository. Detect workspace structure (Go modules, npm workspaces, Cargo workspaces), analyze per-package changes independently, support independent versioning per package, and coordinate cross-package releases. This addresses the PRD's "Monorepo support gaps" risk (rated High) and is critical for enterprise adoption where monorepos are standard.

features.title: CGP Protocol Wire Format
features.description: Formalize the Change Governance Protocol (CGP) wire format as described in PRD Section 17. Implement CGP message types (change.proposal, change.decision, change.execution_authorized) as structured JSON with versioning. Add CGP endpoints to the MCP server so AI agents can propose changes via the protocol. Create a CGP SDK package that other tools can import to become CGP-compliant. This positions Relicta as the reference implementation of an open governance standard.

features.title: Audience-Aware Release Communication
features.description: Implement the stakeholder communication layer from PRD Section 11. Generate audience-specific release narratives (engineering, product, executive, external) derived from approved governance decisions. Support bundling changes across components into coherent narratives. Add communication templates with configurable tone and detail level. Integrate with existing AI providers for narrative generation. This moves Relicta from "output" (changelogs) to "outcomes" (stakeholder communication).

features.title: Release Memory and Learning
features.description: Build the historical context system from PRD Section 16.4. Track past incidents, rollbacks, and their root causes. Identify patterns of risky changes across releases. Feed historical outcomes back into risk scoring so future evaluations improve over time. Store release memory in the persistence layer (file or PostgreSQL). Surface insights via the dashboard analytics. This enables Relicta to continuously improve beyond what stateless tools can achieve.

features.title: Dashboard Frontend Separation
features.description: Extract the embedded Vue dashboard into a standalone deployable frontend as described in PRD Section 14.1. Support CDN-friendly deployment (Vercel, CloudFront, S3). Add real-time updates via WebSocket for release progress, approval notifications, and analytics. Build dashboard views for the new analytics data (risk trends, decision distribution, team metrics). The Go backend serves as a standalone API service alongside the CLI.

features.title: Pre-release and Release Channel Support
features.description: Add pre-release versioning (alpha, beta, rc) and release channels (stable, canary, next). Support promoting pre-releases through channels with governance gates at each stage. Track channel-specific policies (e.g., canary requires lower approval threshold than stable). This addresses the PRD's "Missing critical workflows (pre-release)" gap identified in the product strategy review.

features.title: Multi-Repository Governance
features.description: Coordinate release governance across multiple separate repositories that form a product or platform. Define repository groups with dependency relationships, synchronize version constraints across repos, enforce cross-repo release policies (e.g., "service-api must release before service-client"), and provide a unified view of multi-repo release state. Support both centralized governance (one Relicta instance governs all repos) and federated governance (each repo has Relicta, coordinated via CGP messages). Integrate with the existing CGP protocol for cross-repo proposal/decision exchange.

features.title: Runtime Observability Integration
features.description: Connect post-deployment outcomes back to the release memory system for continuous learning. Integrate with observability platforms (Prometheus, Datadog, PagerDuty, Sentry) to automatically detect incidents, error rate spikes, and rollbacks that correlate with specific releases. Auto-record outcomes in the release memory when deployment metrics cross configured thresholds. Surface deployment health in the dashboard with release-correlated metrics. This closes the feedback loop so Relicta's risk scoring improves with real production data rather than relying solely on code analysis.

constraints.description: File-based persistence remains the default. PostgreSQL is opt-in via config.
Existing file-based deployments must continue working without migration.
Use sqlc for type-safe query generation against PostgreSQL. No ORM dependencies.
Existing API key auth and unversioned endpoints continue working during transition.
PostgreSQL driver is included in the binary. No external runtime dependencies beyond the database itself.
All new packages must meet 80%+ test coverage before merge.
